paragraphs: Rabbi Elazar ben Yehudah of Kefar Bartota, Avot, chapter 3. In Yehoshua’s name, Tevul Yom 3:4, 5; Pesachim 13a, a law from Yehoshua; Bekhorot 57, end of a: son of Rabbi Yehudah from Yehoshua; Akiva said, “I heard,” etc. Orlah 1:4: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel in his name [the checked Mishnah reads Rabban Gamliel]. Maimonides says he appears only in Orlah, chapter 1. Challah, at ע״ח; Shimon ben Elazar in his name; Oholot, at מ״ח; Zavim, at קמ״ב [locators unresolved]. His piety, the miracle filling his house with wheat [the Bavli specifies his storehouse], and charity collectors fleeing him because he gave everything he owned: Seder Ta'aniyot 24a. Yuchasin, end of the chronological section, suggests he was unordained, but all the above places call him Rabbi Elazar. His burial is at Kefar Batra'ah, Gelilot Eretz Yisrael.
